title: Present Value of an Ordinary Annuity

back: The lump‑sum amount today that is equivalent to a series of equal future payments, given an interest rate.
$$PV = \text{Payment} \times \text{PV Annuity Factor}$$
[[imp:PV is always less than the total of all future payments.]]
cards.front: What is the [[kw:present value of an ordinary annuity]]?

back: 1. Determine i (periodic rate) and n (number of payments).
2. Look up the PV annuity factor in the table.
3. Multiply the periodic payment by the factor.
$$PV = \text{Payment} \times \text{PV Annuity Factor}$$
cards.front: How do you find the present value of an ordinary annuity using tables?
Why is the PV of an annuity less than the sum of its payments?
back: Because money received in the future is worth less today due to the time value of money.
Each future payment is discounted back to its present value.
The sum of discounted values is less than the simple sum of payments.

cards.front: Find PV of $1,000 per year for 3 years at 5%. (PV factor = 2.7232)
back: Total payments = $3,000; PV is $276.80 less.
The PV factor decreases.
Higher rate discounts future payments more heavily, reducing their present value.

Compare [[kw:PV of a lump sum]] and [[kw:PV of an annuity]].
back: Lump sum: $$PV = FV \times (1 + i)^{-n}$$ (single future amount).
Annuity: $$PV = \text{Payment} \times \text{PV Annuity Factor}$$ (series of payments).
Use the correct table for each.
The annuity factor is the sum of several lump‑sum PV factors for different periods.
It accumulates the present values of multiple payments, not just one.
cards.front: Why is the annuity PV factor much larger than a lump‑sum PV factor?

back: 1. Understand: identify payment, rate, frequency, and number of periods.
2. Solve: compute i and n, find PV annuity factor, then PV = Payment × Factor.
3. Conclude: verify that the balance would be $0 after all withdrawals.

If the PV of an annuity is $12,000 and the total payments are $15,000, what is the total discount (interest) earned?
back: Discount = Total payments – PV = $15,000 – $12,000 = $3,000.
This $3,000 represents the interest earned by the invested PV over the annuity term.
